description: Creates, updates or destroys an Amazon Elastic Load Balancer (ELB).

parameters.name: access_key
parameters.description: AWS access key ID. See the AWS documentation for more information about access tokens https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws-sec-cred-types.html#access-keys-and-secret-access-keys. The AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID or AWS_ACCESS_KEY environment variables may also be used in decreasing order of preference. The aws_access_key and profile options are mutually exclusive. The aws_access_key_id alias was added in release 5.1.0 for consistency with the AWS botocore SDK.

parameters.name: access_logs
parameters.description: A dictionary of access logs configuration settings (see examples).

parameters.name: aws_ca_bundle
parameters.description: The location of a CA Bundle to use when validating SSL certificates. The AWS_CA_BUNDLE environment variable may also be used.

parameters.name: aws_config
parameters.description: A dictionary to modify the botocore configuration. Parameters can be found in the AWS documentation https://botocore.amazonaws.com/v1/documentation/api/latest/reference/config.html#botocore.config.Config.

parameters.name: connection_draining_timeout
parameters.description: Wait a specified timeout allowing connections to drain before terminating an instance. Set to 0 to disable connection draining.

parameters.name: cross_az_load_balancing
parameters.description: Distribute load across all configured Availability Zones. Defaults to false. Choices: false true

parameters.name: debug_botocore_endpoint_logs
parameters.description: Use a botocore.endpoint logger to parse the unique (rather than total) "resource:action" API calls made during a task, outputing the set to the resource_actions key in the task results. Use the aws_resource_action callback to output to total list made during a playbook. The ANSIBLE_DEBUG_BOTOCORE_LOGS environment variable may also be used. Choices: false ← (default) true

parameters.name: endpoint_url
parameters.description: URL to connect to instead of the default AWS endpoints. While this can be used to connection to other AWS-compatible services the amazon.aws and community.aws collections are only tested against AWS. The AWS_URL environment variable may also be used.

parameters.name: health_check
parameters.description: A dictionary of health check configuration settings (see examples).

parameters.name: idle_timeout
parameters.description: ELB connections from clients and to servers are timed out after this amount of time.

parameters.name: instance_ids
parameters.description: List of instance ids to attach to this ELB.

parameters.name: listeners
parameters.description: List of ports/protocols for this ELB to listen on (see examples). Required when state=present and the ELB doesn’t exist.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the ELB. The name of an ELB must be less than 32 characters and unique per-region per-account.

parameters.name: profile
parameters.description: A named AWS profile to use for authentication. See the AWS documentation for more information about named profiles https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-configure-profiles.html. The AWS_PROFILE environment variable may also be used. The profile option is mutually exclusive with the aws_access_key, aws_secret_key and session_token options.

parameters.name: purge_instance_ids
parameters.description: Purge existing instance ids on ELB that are not found in instance_ids. Choices: false ← (default) true

parameters.name: purge_listeners
parameters.description: Purge existing listeners on ELB that are not found in listeners. Choices: false true ← (default)

parameters.name: purge_subnets
parameters.description: Purge existing subnets on the ELB that are not found in subnets. Because it is not permitted to add multiple subnets from the same availability zone, subnets to be purged will be removed before new subnets are added. This may cause a brief outage if you try to replace all subnets at once. Choices: false ← (default) true

parameters.name: purge_tags
parameters.description: If purge_tags=true and tags is set, existing tags will be purged from the resource to match exactly what is defined by tags parameter. If the tags parameter is not set then tags will not be modified, even if purge_tags=True. Tag keys beginning with aws: are reserved by Amazon and can not be modified. As such they will be ignored for the purposes of the purge_tags parameter. See the Amazon documentation for more information https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws_tagging.html#tag-conventions. Choices: false true ← (default)

parameters.name: purge_zones
parameters.description: Purge existing availability zones on ELB that are not found in zones. Choices: false ← (default) true

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: The AWS region to use. For global services such as IAM, Route53 and CloudFront, region is ignored. The AWS_REGION environment variable may also be used. See the Amazon AWS documentation for more information http://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/rande.html#ec2_region.

parameters.name: scheme
parameters.description: The scheme to use when creating the ELB. For a private VPC-visible ELB use internal. If you choose to update your scheme with a different value the ELB will be destroyed and a new ELB created. Defaults to scheme=internet-facing. Choices: "internal" "internet-facing"

parameters.name: secret_key
parameters.description: AWS secret access key. See the AWS documentation for more information about access tokens https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws-sec-cred-types.html#access-keys-and-secret-access-keys. The AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY or AWS_SECRET_KEY environment variables may also be used in decreasing order of preference. The secret_key and profile options are mutually exclusive. The aws_secret_access_key alias was added in release 5.1.0 for consistency with the AWS botocore SDK.

parameters.name: security_group_ids
parameters.description: A list of security groups to apply to the ELB.

parameters.name: security_group_names
parameters.description: A list of security group names to apply to the ELB.

parameters.name: session_token
parameters.description: AWS STS session token for use with temporary credentials. See the AWS documentation for more information about access tokens https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws-sec-cred-types.html#access-keys-and-secret-access-keys. The AWS_SESSION_TOKEN environment variable may also be used. The session_token and profile options are mutually exclusive.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Create or destroy the ELB. Choices: "absent" "present"

parameters.name: stickiness
parameters.description: A dictionary of stickiness policy settings. Policy will be applied to all listeners (see examples).

parameters.name: subnets
parameters.description: A list of VPC subnets to use when creating the ELB. Mutually exclusive with zones.

parameters.name: tags
parameters.description: A dictionary representing the tags to be applied to the resource. If the tags parameter is not set then tags will not be modified.

parameters.name: validate_certs
parameters.description: When set to false, SSL certificates will not be validated for communication with the AWS APIs. Setting validate_certs=false is strongly discouraged, as an alternative, consider setting aws_ca_bundle instead. Choices: false true ← (default)

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description: When creating, deleting, or adding instances to an ELB, if wait=true Ansible will wait for both the load balancer and related network interfaces to finish creating/deleting. Support for waiting when adding instances was added in release 2.1.0. Choices: false ← (default) true

parameters.name: wait_timeout
parameters.description: Used in conjunction with wait. Number of seconds to wait for the ELB to be terminated. A maximum of 600 seconds (10 minutes) is allowed. Default: 180

parameters.name: zones
parameters.description: List of availability zones to enable on this ELB. Mutually exclusive with subnets.

examples:
# Note: None of these examples set aws_access_key, aws_secret_key, or region.
# It is assumed that their matching environment variables are set.

# Basic provisioning example (non-VPC)

- amazon.aws.elb_classic_lb:
    name: "test-please-delete"
    state: present
    zones:
      - us-east-1a
      - us-east-1d
    listeners:
      - protocol: http # options are http, https, ssl, tcp
        load_balancer_port: 80
        instance_port: 80
        proxy_protocol: true
      - protocol: https
        load_balancer_port: 443
        instance_protocol: http # optional, defaults to value of protocol setting
        instance_port: 80
        # ssl certificate required for https or ssl
        ssl_certificate_id: "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:server-certificate/company/servercerts/ProdServerCert"

# Internal ELB example

- amazon.aws.elb_classic_lb:
    name: "test-vpc"
    scheme: internal
    state: present
    instance_ids:
      - i-abcd1234
    purge_instance_ids: true
    subnets:
      - subnet-abcd1234
      - subnet-1a2b3c4d
    listeners:
      - protocol: http # options are http, https, ssl, tcp
        load_balancer_port: 80
        instance_port: 80

# Configure a health check and the access logs
- amazon.aws.elb_classic_lb:
    name: "test-please-delete"
    state: present
    zones:
      - us-east-1d
    listeners:
      - protocol: http
        load_balancer_port: 80
        instance_port: 80
    health_check:
      ping_protocol: http # options are http, https, ssl, tcp
      ping_port: 80
      ping_path: "/index.html" # not required for tcp or ssl
      response_timeout: 5 # seconds
      interval: 30 # seconds
      unhealthy_threshold: 2
      healthy_threshold: 10
    access_logs:
      interval: 5 # minutes (defaults to 60)
      s3_location: "my-bucket" # This value is required if access_logs is set
      s3_prefix: "logs"

# Ensure ELB is gone
- amazon.aws.elb_classic_lb:
    name: "test-please-delete"
    state: absent

# Ensure ELB is gone and wait for check (for default timeout)
- amazon.aws.elb_classic_lb:
    name: "test-please-delete"
    state: absent
    wait: true

# Ensure ELB is gone and wait for check with timeout value
- amazon.aws.elb_classic_lb:
    name: "test-please-delete"
    state: absent
    wait: true
    wait_timeout: 600

# Normally, this module will purge any listeners that exist on the ELB
# but aren't specified in the listeners parameter. If purge_listeners is
# false it leaves them alone
- amazon.aws.elb_classic_lb:
    name: "test-please-delete"
    state: present
    zones:
      - us-east-1a
      - us-east-1d
    listeners:
      - protocol: http
        load_balancer_port: 80
        instance_port: 80
    purge_listeners: false

# Normally, this module will leave availability zones that are enabled
# on the ELB alone. If purge_zones is true, then any extraneous zones
# will be removed
- amazon.aws.elb_classic_lb:
    name: "test-please-delete"
    state: present
    zones:
      - us-east-1a
      - us-east-1d
    listeners:
      - protocol: http
        load_balancer_port: 80
        instance_port: 80
    purge_zones: true

# Creates a ELB and assigns a list of subnets to it.
- amazon.aws.elb_classic_lb:
    state: present
    name: 'New ELB'
    security_group_ids: 'sg-123456, sg-67890'
    subnets: 'subnet-123456,subnet-67890'
    purge_subnets: true
    listeners:
      - protocol: http
        load_balancer_port: 80
        instance_port: 80

# Create an ELB with connection draining, increased idle timeout and cross availability
# zone load balancing
- amazon.aws.elb_classic_lb:
    name: "New ELB"
    state: present
    connection_draining_timeout: 60
    idle_timeout: 300
    cross_az_load_balancing: "yes"
    zones:
      - us-east-1a
      - us-east-1d
    listeners:
      - protocol: http
        load_balancer_port: 80
        instance_port: 80

# Create an ELB with load balancer stickiness enabled
- amazon.aws.elb_classic_lb:
    name: "New ELB"
    state: present
    zones:
      - us-east-1a
      - us-east-1d
    listeners:
      - protocol: http
        load_balancer_port: 80
        instance_port: 80
    stickiness:
      type: loadbalancer
      enabled: true
      expiration: 300

# Create an ELB with application stickiness enabled
- amazon.aws.elb_classic_lb:
    name: "New ELB"
    state: present
    zones:
      - us-east-1a
      - us-east-1d
    listeners:
      - protocol: http
        load_balancer_port: 80
        instance_port: 80
    stickiness:
      type: application
      enabled: true
      cookie: SESSIONID

# Create an ELB and add tags
- amazon.aws.elb_classic_lb:
    name: "New ELB"
    state: present
    zones:
      - us-east-1a
      - us-east-1d
    listeners:
      - protocol: http
        load_balancer_port: 80
        instance_port: 80
    tags:
      Name: "New ELB"
      stack: "production"
      client: "Bob"

# Delete all tags from an ELB
- amazon.aws.elb_classic_lb:
    name: "New ELB"
    state: present
    zones:
      - us-east-1a
      - us-east-1d
    listeners:
      - protocol: http
        load_balancer_port: 80
        instance_port: 80
    tags: {}

return_values.name: elb
return_values.description: Original boto-style Load Balancer attributes. Returned: always

return_values.name: app_cookie_policy
return_values.description: The name of the policy used to control if the ELB is using a application cookie stickiness policy. Returned: when state=present Sample: "ec2-elb-lb-AppCookieStickinessPolicyType"

return_values.name: backends
return_values.description: A description of the backend policy applied to the ELB (instance-port:policy-name). Returned: when state=present Sample: "8181:ProxyProtocol-policy"

return_values.name: connection_draining_timeout
return_values.description: The maximum time, in seconds, to keep the existing connections open before deregistering the instances. Returned: when state=present Sample: 25

return_values.name: cross_az_load_balancing
return_values.description: Either "yes" if cross-AZ load balancing is enabled, or "no" if cross-AZ load balancing is disabled. Returned: when state=present Sample: "yes"

return_values.name: dns_name
return_values.description: The DNS name of the ELB. Returned: when state=present Sample: "internal-ansible-test-935c585850ac-1516306744.us-east-1.elb.amazonaws.com"

return_values.name: health_check
return_values.description: A dictionary describing the health check used for the ELB. Returned: when state=present

return_values.name: healthy_threshold
return_values.description: The number of consecutive successful health checks before marking an instance as healthy. Returned: success Sample: 2

return_values.name: interval
return_values.description: The time, in seconds, between each health check. Returned: success Sample: 10

return_values.name: target
return_values.description: The Protocol, Port, and for HTTP(S) health checks the path tested by the health check. Returned: success Sample: "TCP:22"

return_values.name: timeout
return_values.description: The time, in seconds, after which an in progress health check is considered failed due to a timeout. Returned: success Sample: 5

return_values.name: unhealthy_threshold
return_values.description: The number of consecutive failed health checks before marking an instance as unhealthy. Returned: success Sample: 2

return_values.name: hosted_zone_id
return_values.description: The ID of the Amazon Route 53 hosted zone for the load balancer. Returned: when state=present Sample: "Z35SXDOTRQ7X7K"

return_values.name: hosted_zone_name
return_values.description: The DNS name of the load balancer when using a custom hostname. Returned: when state=present Sample: "ansible-module.example"

return_values.name: idle_timeout
return_values.description: The length of of time before an idle connection is dropped by the ELB. Returned: when state=present Sample: 50

return_values.name: in_service_count
return_values.description: The number of instances attached to the ELB in an in-service state. Returned: when state=present Sample: 1

return_values.name: instance_health
return_values.description: A list of dictionaries describing the health of each instance attached to the ELB. Returned: when state=present

return_values.name: description
return_values.description: A human readable description of why the instance is not in service. Returned: when state=present Sample: "N/A"

return_values.name: instance_id
return_values.description: The ID of the instance. Returned: when state=present Sample: "i-03dcc8953a03d6435"

return_values.name: reason_code
return_values.description: A code describing why the instance is not in service. Returned: when state=present Sample: "N/A"

return_values.name: state
return_values.description: The current service state of the instance. Returned: when state=present Sample: "InService"

return_values.name: instances
return_values.description: A list of the IDs of instances attached to the ELB. Returned: when state=present Sample: ["i-03dcc8953a03d6435"]

return_values.name: lb_cookie_policy
return_values.description: The name of the policy used to control if the ELB is using a cookie stickiness policy. Returned: when state=present Sample: "ec2-elb-lb-LBCookieStickinessPolicyType"

return_values.name: listeners
return_values.description: A list of lists describing the listeners attached to the ELB. The nested list contains the listener port, the instance port, the listener protoco, the instance port, and where appropriate the ID of the SSL certificate for the port. Returned: when state=present Sample: [[22, 22, "TCP", "TCP"], [80, 8181, "HTTP", "HTTP"]]

return_values.name: name
return_values.description: The name of the ELB. This name is unique per-region, per-account. Returned: when state=present Sample: "ansible-test-935c585850ac"

return_values.name: out_of_service_count
return_values.description: The number of instances attached to the ELB in an out-of-service state. Returned: when state=present Sample: 0

return_values.name: proxy_policy
return_values.description: The name of the policy used to control if the ELB operates using the Proxy protocol. Returned: when the proxy protocol policy exists. Sample: "ProxyProtocol-policy"

return_values.name: region
return_values.description: The AWS region in which the ELB is running. Returned: always Sample: "us-east-1"

return_values.name: scheme
return_values.description: Whether the ELB is an 'internal' or a 'internet-facing' load balancer. Returned: when state=present Sample: "internal"

return_values.name: security_group_ids
return_values.description: A list of the IDs of the Security Groups attached to the ELB. Returned: when state=present Sample: ["sg-0c12ebd82f2fb97dc", "sg-01ec7378d0c7342e6"]

return_values.name: status
return_values.description: A minimal description of the current state of the ELB. Valid values are 'exists', 'gone', 'deleted', 'created'. Returned: always Sample: "exists"

return_values.name: subnets

return_values.name: tags
return_values.description: A dictionary describing the tags attached to the ELB. Returned: when state=present Sample: {"ExampleTag": "Example Value", "Name": "ansible-test-935c585850ac"}

return_values.name: unknown_instance_state_count
return_values.description: The number of instances attached to the ELB in an unknown state. Returned: when state=present Sample: 0

return_values.name: zones
return_values.description: A list of the AWS regions in which the ELB is running. Returned: when state=present Sample: ["us-east-1b", "us-east-1a"]

return_values.name: load_balancer
return_values.description: Boto3-style Load Balancer attributes. Returned: always

return_values.name: availability_zone

return_values.name: backend_server_descriptions

return_values.name: created_time

return_values.name: listener
return_values.description: The listener. Returned: when state=present

return_values.name: instance_protocol

return_values.name: load_balancer_port
